notes: Corrected: מִזְרְחָה הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ → *on the east side* now divides as the directive he taking *on* (rule 32), the article taking *the* (rules 29, 47) and מִזְרָח with שֶׁמֶשׁ sharing *east side* under rule 30, headed on מִזְרָח. The accepted alignment marked both the article and שֶׁמֶשׁ unrepresented, which rule 30's closing sentences forbid where one English word stands for the whole expression.
*there is* is placed on the prepositional predicate בְּשִׁלוֹ under rules 20 and 49; the competing existential reading would put it on חַג.
The ASV margin's *the feast* was read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).
